title: Pro-Scout Identity Requests Document
description: The batch a capture canvas exports for every name it could NOT resolve against its own index. Pro-Scout is the consumer, so Pro-Scout declares what it is able to read; the producer vendors this file and validates its output against it, so neither side restates the other's shape. Required fields are only what Phase 1 genuinely needs -- request_id, which is the join key the search ledger quotes back, and player_name, which is the search input. Everything else is optional and additional properties are permitted throughout: the producer must stay free to add a field (team_hint_as_written arrived exactly that way) without the consumer refusing the batch. Definitions are inlined rather than referenced: the validator this contract is checked with implements no $ref, so an indirection would silently enforce nothing.

schema_version.description: Producer's format version. The pattern admits any major version so this file does not churn; which majors are actually supported is the parser's call, and it says so by name when it refuses one.

team_hint_as_written.description: The spelling the source used, before the canvas normalised it to a club code. A relocation spelling is what tells a search the source is stale, so the code must not be the only thing that travels.

team_hint_basis.description: Where a hint came from. Only an observed value may ever become a fact; a document-scope value describes the document, not the player; an analyst value was typed into the canvas. A basis outside this set means the producer changed its semantics, which is a reason to stop.

position_hint_basis.description: Where a hint came from. Only an observed value may ever become a fact; a document-scope value describes the document, not the player; an analyst value was typed into the canvas. A basis outside this set means the producer changed its semantics, which is a reason to stop.

retained_candidates.description: Candidates the canvas held but could not choose between. Present only on a row it flagged for review.

hint_conflict.description: A hint that contradicted the canvas's own index. It travels unresolved: the search needs to know the disagreement exists, not to have it decided for it.
